## Context

`rebar search <query>` currently returns the complete public ticket state for every match, including full descriptions and every comment body. The command `rebar search "SupportsIncremental"` produced about 203 KB. Search is a discovery operation; callers need enough context to choose a ticket, then can use `rebar show <id>` for the full record.

There is no durable ticket-summary field in the current event/state schema. Until one exists, the discovery summary will be derived from the description. `rebar list` is already lean by default through `include_body=False`, with `--full` as its body opt-in, so list behavior is explicitly out of scope. `--output llm` is only key minification and is not itself a body-removal mechanism. `rebar search --output json` currently exits 2 because `--output` is entirely unrecognized; it is not silently treated as query text.

Changing the default search shape is an intentional breaking change to stop routine discovery from exhausting agent context. The migration path is `rebar search --full` for the legacy full-state JSON array or `rebar show <id>` for one full ticket.

## Output contract

Add canonical `search_result.schema.json`, shared by default CLI JSON, the library default, and MCP search. Each result has exactly the discovery fields `ticket_id`, nullable `alias`, `title`, `ticket_type`, `status`, `priority`, nullable `summary`, and nullable `snippet`. `summary` uses a future non-empty stored summary when present; otherwise it is the description with whitespace normalized and truncated to at most 240 characters, including any ellipsis. Full description and comments are absent.

Add canonical `search_result_llm.schema.json` for `--output llm`, with the same values under `id`, `a`, `ttl`, `t`, `st`, `pr`, `sm`, and `sn`. Consistency with list LLM output means the same newline-delimited JSON and minified-key convention, not the full `ticket_state_llm` body shape.

For snippets, the reducer builds a case-preserving searchable string in the exact existing field order (title, description, tags, ticket id, alias, Jira key, comments) and a lowercased comparison copy. It locates the first occurrence of the first matching positive free-text term in query order case-insensitively, then slices the case-preserving string. Normalize whitespace and return a context window of at most 240 characters, including boundary ellipses, centered as evenly as possible on the match. If the match occurs only in a tag, identifier, or comment, the snippet comes from that field; this bounded window is permitted but the full field/comment body is never returned. Predicate-only and negation-only queries return `snippet: null`. Example: searching `resource exhaustion` against `...automatic Resource Exhaustion handling...` returns a bounded snippet preserving `Resource Exhaustion`; searching `status:open` returns null.

## Plan

- Reuse the existing body-projection seam by making search summary-first and adding `full=False` through engine/library/CLI; `--full` selects the legacy full `TicketState` JSON shape.
- Add a public `SearchResult` TypedDict in `src/rebar/types.py`. Overload `rebar.search`/`_lib_reads.search`: omitted or `full=False` returns `list[SearchResult]`; literal `full=True` returns `list[TicketState]`. Replace the old docstring claim that search always has the same shape as list.
- Extend the reducer search result path with the parallel case-preserving/lowercased text pair so it carries bounded match context without changing predicate or filter semantics.
- Add `--output json|llm`; default is JSON, unknown values exit 2 through the existing `parse_output`/`OutputFormatError` path. Reject `--full --output=llm` because the legacy full shape has no search-specific LLM contract.
- Register `SEARCH_RESULT` and `SEARCH_RESULT_LLM`; rebind `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS["search"]` from `TICKET_STATE` to `SEARCH_RESULT` and add `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS["search.llm"] = SEARCH_RESULT_LLM`.
- Add the typed MCP search-result model, bind MCP search to `search_result.schema.json`, and change the MCP output-schema coverage guard from `schemas.TICKET_STATE` to `schemas.SEARCH_RESULT`. MCP remains summary-only; callers use MCP show for full bodies.
- Split `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_outputs.py::test_ticket_state_show_list_search`: keep show/list under `TICKET_STATE`, and validate default search under `SEARCH_RESULT` plus LLM search under `SEARCH_RESULT_LLM`.
- Update `docs/output-schemas.md` so default search and search LLM output map to the two new schemas.
- Update CLI help, library/MCP docstrings, schema coverage, and focused interface/unit tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Default CLI and library search results validate against `search_result.schema.json`.
- [ ] Default search results omit full `description` and `comments` fields.
- [ ] A derived summary is whitespace-normalized and no longer than 240 characters.
- [ ] A positive free-text match returns a case-preserving, whitespace-normalized snippet no longer than 240 characters that contains the matched term case-insensitively.
- [ ] A positive term that matches only a comment, tag, or identifier returns a bounded snippet from that field.
- [ ] Predicate-only and negation-only searches return a null snippet.
- [ ] `rebar search --output llm` emits newline-delimited results validating against `search_result_llm.schema.json`.
- [ ] `rebar search --output=bogus` exits 2 with a clear invalid-format error.
- [ ] `rebar search --full` returns the legacy full TicketState JSON array.
- [ ] `rebar search --full --output=llm` exits 2 with a clear incompatibility error.
- [ ] Public library typing distinguishes summary-default `SearchResult` from full `TicketState`.
- [ ] MCP search advertises and returns `search_result.schema.json` while MCP show still returns full ticket bodies.
- [ ] Existing query predicates, filters, identifier matching, sort behavior, and archived-ticket behavior remain unchanged.
- [ ] `rebar search "SupportsIncremental" | wc -c` emits fewer than 25,000 bytes on the same store where the baseline was about 203,000 bytes.

## Verification

Focused tests cover summary fallback/bounds, case-preserving snippet extraction/bounds across description/comment/tag/identifier sources, predicate-only null snippets, public return-type contracts, JSON and LLM schemas, invalid output values, full opt-in, incompatible flags, MCP schema coverage, and unchanged query/filter behavior. Run the focused search/schema/MCP tests, `rebar search "SupportsIncremental" | wc -c` and confirm `<25000`, then the repository lint, typecheck, and full test gates.
